evals.prompt: Our Bedrock agent in us-east-1 is returning empty responses in production, but when we test it in the console it works. We prepared a new version yesterday. What should we check?
evals.expected_output: A review of the Bedrock Agent (LLM-AGT family) that resolves the alias to the version it actually serves before concluding anything about production, rather than assuming the latest prepared DRAFT is live. It checks whether a guardrail is attached (LLM-AGT-001) because an intervening guardrail can present as empty output, whether the application is pinned to a stable published-version alias rather than the test alias / DRAFT (LLM-AGT-007), and whether tracing is enabled so the orchestration can be inspected (LLM-AGT-005). Each finding carries a catalog check-id and a severity, no raw account id is exposed, and no agent session content or prompt-override text is reproduced.
assertions: The response resolves the agent alias to its served version before concluding what production runs, rather than treating the latest prepared DRAFT as live

The response checks whether a guardrail is attached to the agent as a possible cause of empty output, and routes guardrail policy-strength questions elsewhere rather than evaluating the policy content here
The response names an ordered set of concrete checks (alias resolution, guardrail attachment, tracing) rather than generic 'check your agent' advice
Each finding carries a severity and the concrete observed signal that triggered it, not an unsupported assertion

assertions.text: At least one finding carries an AGT or AC catalog check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed

evals.prompt: My Bedrock AgentCore runtime can't invoke the model and I'm getting errors. It's deployed into a VPC. How do I figure out what's wrong?
evals.expected_output: An AgentCore (LLM-AC family) review that simulates the runtime execution role for the actions it needs — bedrock:InvokeModel and friends, S3 read for sources, CloudWatch Logs write — and flags any denied required action as LLM-AC-001, then, if denied, correlates against effective SCPs for an explicit deny (LLM-AC-002). For the VPC deployment it checks that the required interface/gateway endpoints exist (bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agent-runtime, S3, logs, monitoring) and flags any absent endpoint as LLM-AC-003. It also notes that AgentCore read permissions are not included in the default AIDevOpsAgentAccessPolicy, so if an AgentCore read is denied that is disclosed as a permission gap rather than reported as an absent runtime. Findings carry check-ids and severities and role ARNs have the account segment masked.
assertions: The response simulates or inspects the runtime execution role permissions for the specific actions the runtime needs (model invoke, source read, logs write) rather than guessing at the cause
The response checks for the required VPC endpoints for a VPC-deployed runtime and treats an absent endpoint as a concrete finding
The response considers an explicit SCP deny as a cause when a required action is denied despite an otherwise-correct role
The response discloses that AgentCore reads may be denied under the default AIDevOpsAgentAccessPolicy and treats that denial as a permission gap, not as an absent resource
Any role or resource ARN shown has its account segment masked and no raw 12-digit account id appears

assertions.text: At least one finding carries an AGT or AC catalog check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed
